details:
Space Mind is a web application prototype designed to support the daily monitoring of stress and well-being among astronauts during missions involving confinement. It allows for the manual entry of three salivary cortisol measurements—taken in the morning, afternoon, and evening—as well as self-assessments of sleep and neuropsychological well-being. Users can also view a "traffic light" style visual indicator. The application maintains a history and generates charts categorized by astronaut, mission, cortisol measurement time, and sleep-related factors. Data is stored locally on the device.

The proposal integrates biological data with self-assessments to facilitate a quick overview of daily changes, assisting the medical team in their monitoring efforts. The traffic light indicator serves as a guide; it does not provide a diagnosis and is not a substitute for a professional medical evaluation.

Developed as a web application using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, it is designed for use via a web browser on a computer or smartphone. Its innovative approach lies in combining objective measurements and subjective self-assessments into a single tool, with interfaces tailored for both the astronaut and the medical team.

The design accounts for the conditions of confinement, mission routines, ease of data entry, and data privacy. As a next step, the project requires collaboration with the laboratory that produces the SOMABIOCIENCIE test, along with access to the test itself and its compatible reader.
dataRefs: A Multimodal Wearable System for Deep Space Monitoring of Stress and Anxiety
